text:
alex: FYI ran the RoPE scaling matrix for the NTK / linear / YARN variants across Llama-3, Mixtral-8x, and Qwen-7B. quick summary below.
priya: thanks — was this the longctx sweep (8k/16k/32k/64k)?
alex: yup. also toggled KV cache eviction heuristics and two batching modes (continuous vs windowed).
marcus: curious about kernel routing — did you let the runtime pick kernels or forced the MHA fallback?
alex: let runtime pick, but also ran a forced-fp16-kernel run to compare. interestingly, when YARN freq > 1.6x we saw kernel choice flip to fallback kernels for Mixtral at >=32k.
sara: can you paste the perf snippet?
alex: ```
# job 4721 mixtral-8x YARN=1.8 seq=32768
throughput: 94.2 tokens/s
latency p50: 210ms p95: 490ms p99: 900ms
kv_hit_rate: 0.62
active_kv_pages: 148
kernel: fallback_ffn_v2
batched_requests: 18
```
jing: that kernel flip is suspicious — fallback_ffn_v2 has worse attention kernel perf for long seqs. might explain latency spike.
perf-bot: [job 4721] perf regression alert: p95 increased 2.3x vs baseline (mixtral-8x, default rope). link: https://perf.redwood/job/4721
priya: did perplexity move on eval sets? any quality regressions?
alex: small changes. on WikiText eval, NTK linear had +0.8 ppl at 32k for Mixtral, YARN had +1.5 ppl at 64k. Llama-3 showed divergence >2 ppl beyond 48k with YARN. Qwen was the most stable (up to 64k no more than +0.4 ppl).
marcus: sounds like per-model safe ranges: Qwen up to 64k, Mixtral up to 32k for YARN, Llama-3 safe to 48k?
sara: i'd prefer we encode explicit safe-range metadata rather than rely on runtime heuristics only. ops needs clear SLAs.
alex: agreed. proposal in thread: add model_rope_limits to model manifest + runtime check that prevents routing to YARN variant beyond safe limit and falls back to linear or smaller window.
priya: also adjust KV eviction: for Mixtral @32k we need eviction threshold at 0.75 active pages or perms out-of-memory. currently eviction kicks too late.
jing: batching heuristics note: continuous batching increases throughput but amplifies p95 if KV misses are high. windowed batching (max wait 6ms) kept p95 stable in our runs.
marcus: can we get a small checklist for eng-runtime to implement?
sara: +1 on checklist. needed items: reproduce job, add manifest flag, kernel-routing guard, KV eviction tuning, add perf test to CI.
alex: created a repo ticket: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/issues/2491 (WIP). I'll attach raw logs.
perf-bot: [job 4723] reproduced Mixtral-8x YARN=1.8 seq=32768 with forced kernel selection -> throughput improved to 110 tok/s, p95 320ms. conclusion: kernel selection matters more than YARN multiplier alone.
priya: action owners? alex (repro + logs), jing (kernel-routing guard), marcus (kv eviction), sara (SLAs + manifest). I'll assign after standup.
alex: one more: when we forced kv prefetch for top-k attention slices, replication reduced active_kv_pages by ~20% and smoothed p99. patch in my branch: `rope/kv-prefetch-optim`
marcus: neat. any tradeoffs on memory?
alex: +6% peak GPU mem but cut tail latency. worth it for Dedicated customers that pay for p99.
sara: OK. let's keep YARN experiments in staging only until guards are in. we don't want surprise regressions in hosted. :warning:
priya: noted. i'll update the rollout doc and console flags so ops can opt-out per-customer.
jing: i'll start a small kernel perf matrix job to find thresholds where runtime should prefer optimized kernels.
alex: thanks. will post final safe-range table here once we finish CI runs.
priya: quick draft safe-range table (preliminary): Mixtral-8x: YARN <= 1.6 -> seq <= 32k; Llama-3-70B: YARN <= 1.4 -> seq <= 48k; Qwen-7B: YARN <= 1.9 -> seq <= 64k. subject to CI verification.
sara: perfect. end-to-end owners noted. tagging this thread to the incident if anything regresses.
perf-bot: archival note: attached perf artifacts -> s3://redwood-perf/rope/1813456789/*
alex: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the ticket and a short RFC on model_rope_limits.
